final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest LOF-proxy pathogenicity (0.998) and extreme intolerance to proline at a conserved Gly in the catalytic domain make this a strongly disruptive loss-of-function substitution.
Very high pathogenicity (0.996), low mutant frequency, and good MSA coverage indicate a functionally important conserved residue whose alanine substitution should abolish activity.
Pathogenicity 0.995 and low evolutionary tolerance support strong LOF, giving a convergent third candidate for abolishing enzyme activity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 is stable with convergent evidence and further evidence is unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the conserved PLP-binding Schiff-base lysine in CBS; substitution to Ala eliminates internal aldimine formation and abolishes catalysis.
High pathogenicity (0.987) and low mutant frequency (0.056) but slightly lower coverage; strong but not top.
Arg cannot form the PLP Schiff base despite retaining positive charge, abolishing cofactor covalent attachment and activity.
Conservative K→R substitution scores much lower pathogenicity (0.777) than K119A, suggesting weaker LOF; demote.
Thr257 lies in the conserved TSGN catalytic/substrate-binding loop of the PLP fold; mutation disrupts PLP phosphate/substrate coordination reducing activity.
Pathogenicity 0.913 is solid but lower than the top group; keep as backup pending MSA.
Asn149 in the conserved active-site region contributes to PLP/substrate positioning; disruption impairs catalysis.
Very high pathogenicity (0.996) with low mutant frequency (0.082) and good MSA coverage (0.977), consistent with functionally important conserved residue.
Conserved Gly in the flexible TSGN catalytic loop; proline substitution rigidifies the loop and disrupts active-site geometry.
Highest pathogenicity (0.998) plus extreme evolutionary intolerance (P freq 0.012); proline in a conserved Gly position of the catalytic domain is strongly disruptive.
Charged conserved residue implicated in substrate/regulatory contacts; neutralization may impair catalytic productivity.
Pathogenicity 0.957 supports LOF but no MSA evidence yet; keep as backup.
Conserved active-site acidic residue potentially involved in catalysis or cofactor contacts; charge removal likely reduces activity.
Predicted benign (0.330), inconsistent with the LOF objective; drop.

rejection.reason: Predicted benign (0.330), inconsistent with the LOF objective; drop.

history.rationale: Aromatic conserved residue near PLP pocket that may stack with the cofactor; disruption can impair binding and catalysis.
Pathogenicity 0.995 and low evolutionary tolerance (A freq 0.026) support LOF; strong convergent signal.
